datum_evidence_reviews.evidence: The Geoscience Australia NGSA Field Manual defines Latitude_GDA94 and Longitude_GDA94 as the site coordinates captured in GDA94. The atlas CSV points to the matching field-site-information product and retains those protocol coordinates as LATITUDE and LONGITUDE.
citations: Geoscience Australia, National Geochemical Survey of Australia: Field Manual, GA Record 2007/08, https://www.ga.gov.au/bigobj/GA10307.pdf (3,443,975 bytes; SHA-256 9f81cf509753ac5abced666e69fa1c166ef35ad1e300c0f52875698f930a60c2), pp. 24-25 field-schema definitions
NGSA atlas CSV metadata row 7 links the field-site-information product eCat 70478; DOI 10.11636/Record.2011.020 retains LATITUDE/LONGITUDE generated by that field protocol
datum_evidence_reviews.fail_closed_behavior: Only source_id australia-ngsa, DOI 10.11636/Record.2011.020 and the exact LATITUDE/LONGITUDE fields may opt in. GDA94 values are carried into canonical EPSG:4326 numerically unchanged under gda94-geographic-wgs84-identity-v1; raw expressions remain preserved and publisher positional accuracy remains not reported.

datum_evidence_reviews.evidence: The NGSA mercury CSV declares its datum in the coordinate column names LATITUDE_GDA94 and LONGITUDE_GDA94; the registered source manifest records the same statement.
citations: NGSA total-Hg product file header, columns LATITUDE_GDA94/LONGITUDE_GDA94 (Geoscience Australia eCat 150328, doi:10.26186/150328)

assets/source_manifest.json sources.australia-ngsa-mercury.coordinate_evidence and scientific_notes bind the GDA94 fields to the registered identity-tolerance policy and preserve publisher positional accuracy as not reported.
datum_evidence_reviews.fail_closed_behavior: GDA94 geographic values are canonicalized to EPSG:4326 numerically unchanged under the registered identity-tolerance policy gda94-geographic-wgs84-identity-v1 (EPSG transformation 1150, +/- 1 m approximation, plate-motion offset under about 2 m against 0.25-degree-or-coarser audit grids). The raw LATITUDE_GDA94/LONGITUDE_GDA94 values remain in every record and every emitted row cites the policy id.

datum_evidence_reviews.evidence: The ESSD data paper states that site coordinates were recorded with a consumer GPS receiver but never names a datum or EPSG code; the TPDC metadata and workbook are also silent.
citations: Wu et al. (2025), ESSD 17, 4779, Sect. 2.1: 'At each site, the geographic coordinate was recorded using a GPS device (eTrex Venture, USA).' (doi:10.5194/essd-17-4779-2025)
TPDC dataset landing page and 'Description of the dataset.docx' (doi:10.11888/Terre.tpdc.302620): no CRS statement
datum_evidence_reviews.fail_closed_behavior: A GPS-device mention is indirect evidence, not a datum declaration; consumer receivers can be configured to non-WGS84 datums. Canonical coordinates stay empty (fail closed); mapping is available only through --coordinate-mode reported with the unverified-datum banner.

datum_evidence_reviews.evidence: GEOROC precompiled documentation describes included 'geospatial coordinates' without any datum or CRS declaration; values are compiled from heterogeneous literature sources.
citations: https://georoc.eu/georoc/precompiled/ ('Files include metadata such as geospatial coordinates, analytical methods, ...'; no datum statement)
assets/source_manifest.json sources.georoc-archaean.scientific_notes: 'Decimal coordinates must not be labeled EPSG:4326 solely from their numeric format.'
datum_evidence_reviews.fail_closed_behavior: Coordinates remain reported-only; no WGS84 bbox filtering and no canonical promotion. This also covers georoc-antarctica-intraplate, whose exact-point subset keeps the same undeclared-datum boundary.

policies.claim: PANGAEA LATITUDE and LONGITUDE geocodes are decimal degrees referenced to WGS84.
limitations: Applies only to exact PANGAEA geocode fields and a PANGAEA dataset DOI.
Does not validate whether a depositor placed values in the correct columns.
Does not apply to renamed, derived, projected, or user-supplied coordinate columns.

policies.claim: EPSG transformation 1150 (GDA94 to WGS 84 (1)) is the registered null geocentric translation for Australia and states an approximation at the +/- 1 m level; plate motion since the 1994 epoch adds less than about 2 m. The finest registered audit grid is 0.25 degrees (roughly 25 km), so declared GDA94 geographic values are carried into canonical EPSG:4326 numerically unchanged under this identity-tolerance policy.
limitations: Applies only to sources whose datum is explicitly declared as GDA94 geographic (EPSG:4283) in publisher metadata or column names.
The identity carry-over is valid for coarse-grid spatial audits and mapping, not for survey-grade positioning; records keep the raw GDA94 values alongside the canonical fields.
Every adapter that opts in must cite this policy_id in its records and its registry notes; silence about the datum keeps a source fail-closed.
A source ID, dataset DOI and coordinate-field pair must match one dataset_bindings entry together; values from separate bindings cannot be combined.
